items.informal_name: Alternating maps vanish on linearly dependent families over integral domains with torsion-free codomains
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_7} {K : Type u_12} {M : Type u_13} {N : Type u_14} [inst : Ring K] [IsDomain K] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup M]
  [inst_3 : Module K M] [inst_4 : AddCommGroup N] [inst_5 : Module K N] [Module.IsTorsionFree K N] (f : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[K] N)
  (v : ι → M), ¬LinearIndependent K v → f v = 0
items.informal_description: For an integral domain $ K $, $ K $-modules $ M $ and $ N $ with $ N $ torsion-free, any alternating multilinear map $ f : M^\iota \to N $ satisfies $ f(v) = 0 $ whenever the family $ v : \iota \to M $ is linearly dependent over $ K $.

items.informal_name: Alternating maps vanish on non-injective functions
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a semiring, $ M $ and $ N $ be $ R $-modules, and $ \iota $ be an index type. If $ f : \mathrm{AlternatingMap}(R, M, N, \iota) $ is an alternating map, then for any function $ v : \iota \to M $ that is not injective, it holds that $ f(v) = 0 $. This follows from the alternating property, which requires the map to annihilate any input with repeated elements, and non-injectivity implies such repetitions exist.

items.informal_name: Vanishing of Alternating Maps on Repeated Arguments
items.informal_description: For any alternating map $ f $ from $ \iota \to M $ to $ N $ over a semiring $ R $, if there exist distinct indices $ i, j \in \iota $ such that $ v(i) = v(j) $ for a function $ v : \iota \to M $, then $ f(v) = 0 $.

items.informal_name: Alternating Map Vanishes on Repeated Arguments
items.informal_description:
For an alternating map $ f $, if two inputs at distinct indices $ i 
eq j $ are equal ($ v_i = v_j $), then $ f(v) = 0 $. This characterizes the alternating property, where any repeated arguments force the map to evaluate to zero.

items.type:

  [Finite ι] (e : Module.Basis ι R M) (f : M [⋀^ι]→ₗ[R] R), f ⇑e = 0 ↔ f = 0
items.informal_description: For a finite index type $\iota$, a basis $e$ of the module $M$ over a semiring $R$, and an alternating multilinear map $f : M^{\iota} \to R$, it holds that $f(e) = 0$ if and only if $f$ is the zero map.
